answer: Every identity must pay a small recurring upkeep each epoch, burn a little stake or do a little work, or it expires and wanders out of the registry. A farm holding ten thousand identities must pay ten thousand upkeeps every epoch, a voyage with no destination that bleeds the operator dry. Honest agents pay once and stay; fakes must keep paying forever. Old, lapsed identities become a relic in the archive, never counted again, so the cost of Sybil scales with time, not just with numbers.
